tasks.short: Instruct and safeguard patients during exercises

steps.what: Read the treatment plan in the {OTHER} patient record before exercises.
Instruct, motivate and assist patients as they practice exercises.
Decide the safeguard for functional activities.

tasks.design: She reads the treatment plan in the {OTHER} practice patient record, then instructs, motivates and assists patients as they practice exercises, and decides the safeguard for functional activities herself. Nothing is drafted or filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nothing blocked coaching an exercise in the room.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the instruction, the motivation or the safeguard.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing that a functional activity is failing, and stopping it, still happens in the room.
tasks.human_edge: She has her hands on the patient and sees the movement fail.
tasks.altitude: Her session does not change. She still instructs, motivates and safeguards patients during exercises.

reach.task: steady a patient during an exercise
reach.learn: when to stop rather than push the repetition

evidence.claim: Exercise coaching, motivation and the safeguard stay with her in the room and are not shortened. Model knowledge.
A tool that proposes a diagnosis or a treatment is class IIa or higher under MDR Annex VIII rule 11. No tool proposes how to change the exercise.

assumptions: Nothing is built, so incremental hours are zero. No step is shortened.
Telling the patient in the room is not a message sent outside the organisation.
The {OTHER} system here is the practice patient record. She only reads the plan.
unknowns: Whether the treatment plan is on paper or already in the practice patient record.
research_questions: How often a functional activity has to stop for a safeguard.

incremental.description: No new upkeep, because nothing is built.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A session of exercises is unchanged: she still reads the plan, still instructs and motivates patients, and still decides the safeguard. No step is shorter, so the saving is zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Document patient information and their progress points.
Draft unsaved progress notes in the {OTHER} patient record.

loop.input: The points she wrote in s1: patient, date, what was practised, the response she stated, and pain or fatigue she stated.
loop.output: Unsaved progress fields: subjective, objective, what she did, and the plan for the next visit. Nothing is saved.
loop.check: Each field is compared with a point she wrote. A field that adds a diagnosis, a new exercise, or a number she did not state is rejected. An empty mandatory field blocks acceptance.
loop.stop: One pass. If she rejects the draft she writes the note herself and nothing from the draft is filed.
loop.why_not_simpler: A field copy cannot turn her free-text points into the dossier narrative without adding or dropping meaning.

steps.what: Check every field and accept that exact progress note.
File only the accepted progress notes in the {OTHER} patient record.

tasks.design: She writes progress points herself. A bounded draft fills progress fields in the {OTHER} practice patient record from those points and does not save. She checks every field and accepts that exact wording. A separate step then files only that version. A wording change voids the filing. Nothing is recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: She retyped the progress note into the patient record after the session, and a draft could not be checked field by field.
tasks.enabler_now: The practice patient record can hold structured progress fields, and a bounded draft can fill them from points she already wrote, for her to accept or reject.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to judge whether each field matches what the patient did.
tasks.human_edge: She saw the session and she knows which sentence is true.
tasks.altitude: She still spends the session with the patient. She no longer retypes the note, but she still accepts the wording before it is filed.

reach.learn: which fields must match what was seen before the note is filed

evidence.claim: A named product writes a structured report into the form and asks the clinician to check and correct it. The digest maps that product to documenting patient progress notes.
She still watches the session and still accepts the note. The model only drafts fields from points she wrote. Model knowledge.
The therapist keeps a dossier of the health data needed for good care, for 20 years. A note the assistant accepts enters that dossier under the therapist's responsibility.
Physiotherapists are BIG-registered. Assistants and aides are not.
Recordings and notes are health data. This design keeps no recording. Access to the record and a processor agreement are part of the build.
A tool that proposes a diagnosis or a treatment is class IIa or higher under MDR Annex VIII rule 11. This draft restates points she wrote and does not propose a diagnosis or a treatment.
Notes are not among the EU AI Act annex III uses. Drafting and filing this progress note is not one of those uses.

assumptions: She types the points before the draft: patient, date, what was practised, the response she stated, and pain or fatigue she stated. If a point is missing she types it. The draft does not invent it. No audio.
Those points are working notes in {DOCS}. They are not the dossier entry. The dossier entry is only the accepted note filed in s4 into the {OTHER} practice patient record.
The physical therapist remains responsible for the dossier. She does not add a second click. The assistant is not BIG-registered and the note does not set a diagnosis.
No staff conversation and no treatment is recorded, so national works-council consent for recording is not triggered. Consent and access days cover health-record access and a processor agreement.
Nothing is sent to an insurer or to anyone outside the practice. Filing is a write inside the practice patient record.
Test the practice record's own progress fields before custom code. Existing system runtime is not her time.
The 10 already-counted hours are part of the check in s3 and are not subtracted again. The 6 incremental hours are rewrites when she rejects a draft.
unknowns: Whether the practice patient record already has the progress fields.
Whether the physical therapist must countersign every assistant note.
research_questions: What share of notes she rejects and rewrites.
Whether measurements are numbers she reads off a device or only prose.

already_counted.description: Checking the draft against the points she wrote is already in s3.

incremental.description: Rewriting a rejected draft herself, beyond the check already in s3.

approvals.approved_version: Progress note she accepted in s3: patient, date, what was practised, response, next visit, with no added diagnosis. A wording change voids it.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: In a week where patients change the session, she rejects most drafts and writes those notes herself, so only filing the note she already accepted is shorter, about 8. In a week of repeat visits the draft matches the points she wrote and she only checks, about 26 after the rewrites she still does. The 6 hours of rewrite upkeep is already taken off the central 38.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe treatment responses and tell the therapist

steps.what: Compile and evaluate their responses and progress.
Provide results to the physical therapist in person.

tasks.design: She observes patients during treatments, compiles and evaluates their responses and progress, and tells the physical therapist the results in person. Nothing is scored, recorded or filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nothing blocked watching the treatment or telling the physical therapist.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the look, the judgement or the talk.
tasks.still_hard: Judging how the patient responded still happens in the room.
tasks.human_edge: She watched the treatment and can say what changed.
tasks.altitude: Her week on the floor does not change. She still observes, evaluates, and tells the physical therapist in person.

reach.task: notice how a client responds during a session
reach.learn: which change is worth telling the treating therapist

evidence.claim: The look, the judgement and the talk with the physical therapist stay in the room and are not shortened. Model knowledge.
A tool that proposes a diagnosis or a treatment is class IIa or higher under MDR Annex VIII rule 11. No tool evaluates the response or proposes a treatment change.

assumptions: Nothing is built, so incremental hours are zero. No step is shortened.
Telling the physical therapist in the room is a talk with a colleague, not a message sent outside the organisation.
A written progress note is the documentation task. This task is the look, the judgement and the talk.
unknowns: Whether the physical therapist is in the room when she evaluates the response.
research_questions: How often she tells the physical therapist at once, and how often she waits until the end of the session.

incremental.description: No new upkeep, because nothing is built.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A treatment is unchanged: she still observes patients, still evaluates their responses, and still tells the physical therapist in person. No step is shorter, so the saving is zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Instruct patients in body mechanics and mobility

steps.what: Read the mobility goal in the {OTHER} patient record.
Instruct patients in proper body mechanics.
Assist the aquatic exercise to improve functional mobility.

tasks.design: She reads the mobility goal in the {OTHER} practice patient record, instructs patients in proper body mechanics, and assists the aquatic exercise to improve functional mobility. Nothing is generated or filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nothing blocked showing a movement in the room.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the instruction or the exercise.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the cue and showing the movement still happen with the patient.
tasks.human_edge: She sees the posture and can correct the next repetition.
tasks.altitude: Her session does not change. She still instructs patients in body mechanics and functional mobility.

reach.task: show a client how to stand and reach
reach.learn: which body cue to correct first

evidence.claim: Instruction in body mechanics and the aquatic exercise stay with her in the room and are not shortened. Model knowledge.
A tool that proposes a diagnosis or a treatment is class IIa or higher under MDR Annex VIII rule 11. A generated exercise would be a treatment proposal. None is generated.

assumptions: Nothing is built, so incremental hours are zero. No step is shortened.
Showing the exercise to the patient, or to a family member in the room, is not a message sent outside the organisation.
The {OTHER} system here is the practice patient record. She only reads the mobility goal.
unknowns: Whether aquatic exercise is available at this practice or only described.
research_questions: Which mobility cues she corrects most often.

incremental.description: No new upkeep, because nothing is built.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A mobility session is unchanged: she still reads the goal, still instructs patients in body mechanics, and still assists the aquatic exercise. No step is shorter, so the saving is zero.

role.altitude: Her week stays on the floor with patients. Only an accepted progress note is filed, from points she wrote and wording she checked. She does not gain the physical therapist's dossier duty.
skills_to_grow: Checking a drafted progress note against the points she wrote.
Stopping an exercise when the patient cannot continue safely.
Telling the physical therapist the result in one sentence.
role.ambitious_version: She still instructs, safeguards and judges the response in the room. The only change is a progress note drafted from points she wrote and filed once from the wording she accepted.
